slot.brief: Give a formula of a simple coordination compound (e.g. ammine/aqua/chloro complex with a cation or anionic complex) and ask for its correct IUPAC name among four close options.

stem: The correct IUPAC name of the coordination compound $\text{K}_2[\text{PtCl}_6]$ is

verdicts.working: The complex ion has charge −2. With six Cl⁻ ligands, Pt is +4; an anionic platinum complex is named platinate. Thus the name is potassium hexachloridoplatinate(IV).

working:
$x+6(-1)=-2 \Rightarrow x=+4$ for Pt.
The complex ion is anionic, so the metal name takes the suffix “-ate”.
Six chlorido ligands give “hexachlorido”.
Name: potassium hexachloridoplatinate(IV).

Independent check: The complex ion has charge −2. With six Cl⁻ ligands, Pt is +4; an anionic platinum complex is named platinate. Thus the name is potassium hexachloridoplatinate(IV).
solution:
Let the oxidation state of Pt be $x$. For $[\text{PtCl}_6]^{2-}$,
$$x+6(-1)=-2 \Rightarrow x=+4.$$
The anionic complex uses the suffix “-ate”; six chlorido ligands give hexachlorido. Hence the name is potassium hexachloridoplatinate(IV).
